text.p: Swedish ferry operator Stena Line said on Thursday that it expected its 1997 result to be better than its 1996 earnings.
"Risks for 1997 are...smaller than in 1996, so this year's result should improve," chief executive Bo Lerenius told the annual general meeting.
In 1996 the group posted a loss of 448 million crowns.
For the first quarter of 1997, Stena Line showed a loss of 493 million crowns compared to a loss of 504 million crowns in the corresponding year earlier quarter.
First quarter sales rose 12 percent, or 186 million crowns, to 1.78 billion crowns with about 100 million crowns of the increase stemming from currency fluctuations, the company said in a statement.
Net debt increased by about 500 million crowns since the year-end, the company added.
The number of passengers rose 18 percent to nearly three million in the first quarter and freight units also increased by 18 percent to 276,000.
On the Dover-Calais route, Stena Line's market share has improved with the number of cars rising 18 percent in the first quarter and the number of freight units advancing 27 percent.
On the English Channel, ticket prices were significantly lower because of the price policies of the competing Channel Tunnel, the group said.
In Scandinavia, ticket prices were unchanged but on the Irish Sea average ticket prices rose.
The company does not publish a full first quarter earnings report.
At 1420 GMT, Stena Line's share was 0.80 crown lower at 33.20.
